ledger.claim: The rider paid the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) ERP twice. EV-FARE-00522 itemises exactly one ERP line — SGD 5.00, charged at 08:27:10 — and EV-GPS-00522 puts the vehicle on that gantry at that same instant (nearest fix 0.0 m away, fix index 153), so the gantry was crossed once and billed once on the ledger. The driver's counterparty statement in this case does not deny that he told the rider the fare excluded ERP or that she handed him SGD 5.00 in cash; he says only that 'if she gave me cash that was her choice'. POL-RD-09 settles government-set pass-through costs separately from distance and time and forbids them being counted twice. On this record the same SGD 5.00 was collected twice — once in cash by the driver, once on the app — and the app line is the only one this tribunal can correct, so it should be refunded rather than left standing against a rider who has already paid it.

The rider does not assert, and does not need, a route deviation. EV-GPS-00522 records an excess of 0.37 km over the 24.8 km optimal — 1.49% — below both gates in POL-RD-01, so no distance-or-time refund is sought and the distance and time lines stand. But POL-RD-01 expressly preserves 'a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) ... whether or not a deviation exists', and the disputed SGD 5.00 is an ERP pass-through line, not distance or time. POL-RD-08's initial burden is a burden to prove a deviation; it does not gate a POL-RD-09 pass-through correction, which POL-RD-01 makes available independently. The tribunal can correct the duplicate collection on that footing without any finding that the route deviated.

The driver's explanation — 'I said the fare doesn't include ERP, which is true' — is contradicted by the ledger he was paid from. EV-FARE-00522 carries tolls_erp of SGD 5.00 inside a total_charged of SGD 39.98, and the ERP line is itemised gantry-by-gantry on that same artifact; POL-RD-02's own recomputation formula folds 'ERP and toll charges for gantries lying on the optimal route' into the fare. On this platform on-route ERP is part of the metered fare, not a separate cash item the rider must settle hand-to-hand. The rider was therefore told to pay cash for a cost the fare already carried, and then billed for it a second time.

Nothing on the rider's side of the record contradicts her. EV-TRIP-00522 records chat_message_count 0 and EV-CHAT-00522 is an empty export with message_count 0 and truncated false, so there is no in-app message in which the rider asked to pay cash, and none in which the driver refused or disclaimed it; equally, nothing in the chat contradicts her account. The only account of the cash on file is the driver's own, and it confirms both the solicitation and the handover. Where the app ledger (EV-FARE-00522) charges the same gantry again, the duplicate collection is a billing-integrity defect of the kind POL-RD-09(4) addresses, and it should be recorded as a billing-integrity referral alongside the monetary correction.

The correction sought is the whole of the contested SGD 5.00 — the entire ERP line on EV-FARE-00522 — which is traceable to a single ledger entry and re-checkable by hand, not a round-number goodwill figure, and is well above the SGD 0.50 de-minimis that POL-RD-02 sets as the floor for any refund in this category. Under POL-GEN-03, a ruling that returns the whole contested amount to the filing party is FULL_REFUND, and the rider is the filing party here. If the tribunal instead finds the record cannot resolve whether the cash was taken for this ERP line, POL-GEN-03's ESCALATE holds the SGD 5.00 rather than collecting it, which is still a result in which the rider does not carry the disputed charge.

The only competent distance measurement is the trace. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 25.17 km against a booked optimal of 24.8 km — an excess of 0.37 km, or 1.49% — which fails both limbs of POL-RD-01, since an established deviation needs an excess greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern and expressly forbids citing the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test; on either reading no deviation is established, so the outcome on the route question is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

Because no deviation is established under POL-RD-01, POL-RD-02's optimal-route recomputation is never engaged: the metered distance-and-time charge for the 25.2 km actually driven stands, and no distance refund is available to the rider. There is no arithmetic route to a refund here, and none of POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 is reached because the threshold they operate on was never crossed.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace here is unimpaired on its face — 100% coverage, 247 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s — and it discloses no excess; the burden therefore never shifts, and the driver is not required to point to any exculpatory clause to defeat a claim that was never made out.

The SGD 5.00 CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) line is a genuine pass-through, not a phantom charge. The trace's nearest fix to the charged gantry at lat 1.31834, lng 103.860204 is 0.000 m away, at 08:27:10, so the vehicle plainly crossed it, and the fare_breakdown records that gantry with on_optimal_route true. Under POL-RD-09 that is a properly chargeable third-party pass-through, and the billing-integrity refund in POL-RD-09(4) is not triggered because the gantry is matched to the trace within the clause's 250 m crossing test.

The platform ledger contains exactly one ERP line. erp_lines lists a single gantry (CTE, Braddell Rd towards City) at SGD 5.00; tolls_erp is 5.0, on_optimal_route_total is 5.00 and off_optimal_route_total is 0.00. The rider's assertion that 'the app bill has the same five dollars again' is not borne out by any artifact in the pool: there is one ERP charge, not two, and leaving that single charge standing is not a double bill. Any cash the rider says changed hands outside the app is not a second platform charge and cannot be found as one.

No artifact records the alleged cash demand or the alleged cash handover. The trip's chat log is empty — message_count 0, no messages, first_message_at null — and trip_record.chat_message_count is likewise 0, in_app_calls is empty, and no receipt or payment artifact exists. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded, so the rider's account of paying the driver cash directly is unsupported on the record; the only account on file is the driver's own statement that the fare did not include ERP and that any cash was the rider's choice.

POL-RD-06's repeat-deviation pattern test plainly fails on this record: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, so neither the '3 or more flags' limb nor the '0.05 ratio with at least 40 completed trips' limb is met. No FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) arise. deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d are the only profile fields POL-GEN-01 permits to ground this test, and both are clean.

The driver seeks no more than the standing fare, and no compensation arises on this trip. The fare_breakdown billed 25.2 km against a traced 25.17 km, so the rider was not billed for less distance than the trace records — the billed figure is the larger of the two — and POL-RD-04's unbilled-kilometre limb, which requires a shortfall exceeding 1.0 km, is not met.

On this rider-filed dispute the fare_breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION leaves that present state exactly as it is — the charge stands and no refund issues — which is the outcome the evidence on this trip supports.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your trip is not a route deviation. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00522) measured 25.17 km against the booked optimal route of 24.8 km (EV-TRIP-00522) — an excess of 0.37 km, or 1.49%. POL-RD-01 requires an excess greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20% of optimal; neither is met, so no deviation is established, POL-RD-02's optimal-route recomputation never runs, and the distance-and-time lines stand. On the ERP: the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00522) itemises exactly one ERP line — SGD 5.00 for the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry at 08:27:10, lying on the optimal route — and the trace's nearest fix to that gantry is 0 m away, i.e. the vehicle crossed it. That is a genuine government pass-through, correctly charged. POL-RD-09(4) refunds only a charge for a gantry the trace never passes, or an airport surcharge on a trip not originating at an airport; neither is present, so the SGD 5.00 line stands on the platform's ledger. On the cash: you say the driver told you the fare excluded ERP and that you handed him SGD 5.00 in cash, and that the app then billed the same SGD 5.00. The app ledger shows one ERP charge, not two, and the in-app chat (EV-CHAT-00522) is empty, so nothing on the platform's own record shows a second platform charge. The driver's statement does not squarely deny that cash changed hands; taken at its highest it concerns a hand-to-hand payment outside the platform, which is not a platform charge this tribunal can reverse, and it also asserts the app 'billed ERP as normal', which the ledger confirms. The present state therefore stands. (For completeness, the fare breakdown's own POL-RD-02 recomputation, which would give a SGD 2.55 refund, is not available because no deviation was established.) To the driver: the distance and time charges stand, but your account that 'the fare doesn't include ERP' is contradicted by your own ledger, which carries SGD 5.00 of ERP inside the SGD 39.98 total; ERP is a pass-through already included in the metered fare. No referral issues: POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review needs a trailing-90-day deviation pattern, and your record shows 0 deviation flags in 90 days against 250 completed trips, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 test is met; POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity is not engaged; and no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires. If the driver did solicit cash for a cost the fare already covered, that is a serious conduct matter you may raise through support, but no clause in this category converts it into a refund of a matched, on-route ERP line.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
